data.narrative:
Medra is a Series A-stage biotech company that has raised $52M to date. The valuation universe comprises 3 public comparables in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals, though none offered sufficient datapoint density for reliable peer-median benchmarking.

Of three triangulation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method uses Medra's $52M total raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to subsequent funding rounds, implying a valuation of $104M. Peer-median analysis was inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or similar-tier comparables within the narrow biotech filter; the 7 same-sector peers lacked the minimum 3 datapoints needed for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring could not be executed because Medra, as a private company, does not disclose revenue—a necessary input given the public Biotech & Health P/S median of 8.1x across the three tickers.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $88M to $120M, with a median of $104M. This range reflects conservative (15% haircut) and optimistic (15% uplift) scenarios around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue visibility, limited private-peer comparability data, and reliance on a generic stage-based multiplier rather than company-specific traction or burn metrics.
